title: Lord! When Thy People Seek Thy Face
description: Lord! When Thy People Seek Thy Face in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 35 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Invoking a Blessing”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! when thy peo-ple seek thy face, And dy-ing sin-ners pray to live, Hear thou in heaven, thy dwell-ing place, And, when thou hear-est, O for-give!

lines: Lord! when thy people seek thy face,
And dying sinners pray to live,
Hear thou in heaven, thy dwelling-place,
And, when thou hearest, O forgive!
The blessed Gospel of thy Son,
Still, by the power of his great name,
Be mighty signs and wonders done.
Here to abide, no transient guest?
Here will the world's Redeemer reign,
And here the Holy Spirit rest?
Yet choose not, Lord, this house alone;
Thy kingdom come to every heart,
In every bosom fix thy throne.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
